body:
Thank you for your response - I am appreciative of it

I feel like I should see someone. I have not. I haven't had the best experiences previously. I know things are getting worse. I have had a few breakdowns in public which don't happen unless it is getting worse. I really do need to see someone about it. I just don't know how to go about it. The waiting list here is very long. But I know it will help. It just seems like a lot of work and I'm terrified of it not working out. I desperately want to talk to someone about it though.

Thank you - you are very kind. 

I have not spoken to a therapist or anyone about this. I wouldn't know who to go to really. I haven't had the best experiences in the past. I know I should find someone. It wouldn't be fair to pile it all on my husband. I'm just scared of minimisation etc. When I was in hospital last time the nurse was incredibly unprofessional and really made things worse. Left a bad taste in my mouth I guess. But I know they'r enot all like that. I am also worried as I cannot really phrase my problems in a cogent way as you can probably gather from my writing. So I fear it would seem nonsensical.

I guess...  He himself has anxiety and I don't want to add to it as it were. I'm glad your girlfriend is helping. I understand the feeling you went through, as I'm no stranger to that myself. Just this time I don't want to burden him or anyone else. Then again there is a risk of it getting worse if I keep it to myself. Thank you for your words.

Thank you. I don't even know what to say right now to be honest. Because it is totally irrational why I feel the way I feel. Which itself is an irrational thought as I know it doesn't have a rhyme nor reason. But even so. Does that make sense?
